rankings.blurb: Six Cornerstones. SIX. Ja'Marr Chase, JSN, Drake London, De'Von Achane, Omarion Hampton, and Jayden Daniels all in one dynasty roster — this is absolutely disgusting and I refuse to look directly at it. The receiver room alone would make grown men weep, and somehow Sven also has Justin Herbert and Trevor Lawrence as BACKUP quarterbacks. The only knock is a thin pick cupboard and some recent trades that look like he was paying a robbery tax to nchernandez, but when your player assets are this elite, you can afford to overpay a little. This is the most terrifying roster in the league and it's not particularly close.

Drake Maye, Jahmyr Gibbs, Puka Nacua, and Trey McBride walking into a room together is genuinely unfair — four elite dynasty assets anchoring a roster that also has Tetairoa McMillan and Cam Ward waiting in the wings. The Gibbs acquisition cost an arm, a leg, and three picks, but getting a 9,911 KTC running back in his prime is the kind of move that wins championships, not just trade grades. The pick shelf is basically empty with only one first rounder, so this is a full-throttle win-now roster — and honestly, it should be. The only thing standing between ekleiner and a title is Sven's grotesque WR room.

Seven first-round picks and a 155K total dynasty value that leads the entire league — on paper, jsinykin is running a masterclass in asset accumulation. Caleb Williams as a Cornerstone QB with Jaxson Dart riding the bench is the kind of quarterback depth that makes other owners physically ill, and Harold Fannin at TE is a sneaky elite stash. The Reload tag is honest though — there's no true RB1 to hang your hat on, and Jeremiyah Love hasn't proven a thing yet in the NFL. This roster is going to be absolutely terrifying in 12-18 months, but right now it's a futures bet more than a title contender.

Josh Allen at 9,998 KTC is the single most valuable player in this entire league, and Ashton Jeanty next to him as a Cornerstone RB gives this team a foundation most owners would sell their soul for. The problem is what surrounds them — Zay Flowers and Jaylen Waddle as your WR2 and WR3 isn't exactly inspiring, and the TE room of Sam LaPorta and Kenyon Sadiq is quietly concerning. Gavin shipped out Tyler Shough and a 2027 first to get Garrett Wilson back, which is a sideways move at best, and the Reload tag feels accurate — great ceiling, but the middle of this roster needs work before this team is truly championship-caliber.

Joe Burrow and Amon-Ra St. Brown as Cornerstones with Jalen Hurts and Jonathan Taylor behind them — this roster has legitimate star power and looks like a playoff team every single week. But the recent trade history is an absolute catastrophe: giving up Jameson Williams, two 2029 firsts, and a second to nchernandez for Malik Willis and Michael Wilson is the kind of transaction that gets you roasted in the group chat for years. Now sitting with zero first-round picks after also shipping a 2027 first to jsinykin for Breece Hall, this team is all-in right now with no margin for error. The window is open but the front door is unlocked and the alarm system is disabled.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers as your top two assets is a genuinely elite core — a 9,999 KTC RB1 and an 8,135 KTC TE1 would make any dynasty owner salivate. nchernandez has also been absolutely robbing people in the trade market lately, fleecing both Sven and GiantHawkTua to stockpile six first-round picks while those suckers handed over futures like candy on Halloween. The issue is that WR is a genuine wasteland — Marvin Harrison is the WR1 and he still hasn't become the player his draft capital suggested — and the QB room of Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, and Geno Smith is one injury away from a disaster. This rebuild is trending in the right direction though, and the pick haul is real.

Selling Ja'Marr Chase — a 9,978 KTC Cornerstone — to go full rebuild is a bold move, and at least Akracoon has seven first-round picks to show for the scorched earth approach. But beyond Malik Nabers as the lone Cornerstone anchor, this roster is genuinely bleak: Fernando Mendoza and Dak Prescott at QB, Bhayshul Tuten as your RB1, and a WR room that drops off a cliff after Nabers. The team name is Skyline Chili Enjoyer, which is already a red flag about this person's judgment, and the tier breakdown confirms it — one Cornerstone and a bunch of Serviceable filler does not a contender make. The picks are the only reason this isn't a bottom-two ranking.

Seth flipped Jahmyr Gibbs for a treasure chest of picks and has been playing 4D chess while everyone else plays checkers — five first-round picks acquired and a 132K dynasty value despite a roster headlined by George Pickens and TreVeyon Henderson. The QB situation is genuinely dire though: Tyler Shough, Aaron Rodgers, and Quinn Ewers is a depth chart that belongs in a support group, not a fantasy playoff race. No Cornerstone players and a Foundational player count of just one means this team is entirely betting on the picks hitting, and with Seth's track record of winning trades, that's not a crazy bet. Just don't expect to win anything in 2026 — this is a 2028 situation at the earliest.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb are two of the best WRs in dynasty, full stop — but they're sitting on a roster with Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Sam Darnold at QB, which is essentially a three-headed monster of mediocrity. The RB room is Christian McCaffrey on his last legs, Saquon Barkley also aging out, and Chase Brown as the only young piece — this team is in a race against time that it appears to be losing. Zero future picks, a total dynasty value that's nearly 50K below the top teams, and a trade history that includes giving up assets for Jerry Jeudy and Cade Otton — none of this screams dynasty powerhouse. The rings in the team name suggest past glory; the roster suggests that glory is firmly in the rearview mirror.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes as your starting QBs is an all-time flex, and yet somehow this roster is ranked dead last — that tells you everything you need to know about how catastrophically thin the rest of the team is. Zero future picks. Zero. Derrick Henry and Josh Jacobs at RB. Travis Kelce and Dallas Goedert at TE. The window this team is trying to jump through is closing fast, and Herschey is standing outside in the cold with a roster that has more aging veterans than a military reunion. The recent trade of a 2028 first and picks for Ladd McConkey is fine, but trading draft capital when you already have none is like spending your last dollar on a lottery ticket — bold, probably dumb, and somehow on-brand.
